arxiv-2405-02566.title: Dirac Brackets ↔ \leftrightarrow Lindblad Equation: A Correspondence
arxiv-2405-02566.creator: Aleek Maity and V V Sreedhar
arxiv-2405-02566.description: Abstract The time evolution of an open quantum system is governed by the Gorini-Kossakowski-Sudarshan-Lindlad equation for the reduced density operator of the system. This operator is obtained from the full density operator of the composite system involving the system itself, the bath, and the interactions between them, by performing a partial trace over the bath degrees of freedom.

arxiv-2412-05444.title: Epidemiology of the Living Dead: A social Force Model of a Zombie Outbreak
arxiv-2412-05444.creator: Sydney Balkovitz, Alyssa Croco, Jake Garda, Maggie Hatch, Franklyn Paul, Lauren Vu, Tristan West and Gavin Buxton Science Department, Robert Morris University, Moon Township, PA 15108, US.
arxiv-2412-05444.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Sydney Balkovitz, Alyssa Croco, Jake Garda, Maggie Hatch, Franklyn Paul, Lauren Vu, Tristan West and Gavin Buxton Science Department, Robert Morris University, Moon Township, PA 15108, US.. We adapt the social force model of crowd dynamics to capture the evacuation during a zombie outbreak from an academic building. Individuals navigate the building, opening doors, and evacuate to the nearest exit.

arxiv-2509-15826.title: Campus AI vs. Commercial AI: How Customizations Shape Trust and Usage of LLM as-a-Service Chatbots DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/2018/06 CCS: Human-centered computing Empirical studies in HCI CCS: Human-centered computing User studies CCS: Human-centered computing Natural language int
arxiv-2509-15826.creator: Leon Hannig, Annika Bush, Meltem Aksoy, Tim Trappen, Steffen Becker, Greta Ontrup
arxiv-2509-15826.description: Abstract . As the use of LLM ( LLM ) chatbots by students and researchers becomes more prevalent, universities are pressed to develop AI strategies. One strategy that many universities pursue is to customize pre-trained LLM as-a-service (LLMaaS). While most studies on LLMaaS chatbots prioritize technical adaptations, we focus on psychological effects of user-salient customizations, such as interface changes.

arxiv-2512-13705.title: Scaling and Transferability of Annealing Strategies in Large Language Model Training
arxiv-2512-13705.creator: Siqi Wang, Zhengyu Chen, Teng Xiao, Zheqi Lv, Jinluan Yang, Xunliang Cai, Jingang Wang, Xiaomeng Li
arxiv-2512-13705.description: Abstract Learning rate scheduling is crucial for training large language models, yet understanding the optimal annealing strategies across different model configurations remains challenging. In this work, we investigate the transferability of annealing dynamics in large language model training and refine a generalized predictive framework for optimizing annealing strategies under the Warmup-Steady-Decay (WSD) scheduler.

pmc-11452714.title: Clinical impacts of concomitant left atrial appendage occlusion during mitral valve surgery in patients with mitral regurgitation
pmc-11452714.creator: Jiwon Seo, Hee-Jung Lee, Iksung Cho, Young Joo Suh, Seung-Hyun Lee, Sak Lee, Geu-Ru Hong, Jong-Won Ha, Young Jin Kim, Chi Young Shim
pmc-11452714.description: Surgical occlusion of the left atrial appendage (LAA) during cardiac surgery in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) is known to reduce thromboembolism. However, data on the clinical significance of LAA occlusion (LAAO) in patients with mitral regurgitation (MR) are lacking. A total of 237 AF patients with chronic severe MR who underwent mitral valve (MV) surgery were retrospectively analyzed.

pmc-12553573.title: A novel fourth generation of CAR-T cells: CD19 CAR-T cells engineered to express membrane-bound interleukin-15 and CXCR5 for the treatment of lymphoma
pmc-12553573.creator: Xinping Cao, Jile Liu, Mohan Zhao, Shujing Guo, Meng Zhang, Xiaomei Zhang, Rui Sun, Yifan Zhao, Ruiting Guo, Yi Zhang, Mingfeng Zhao
pmc-12553573.description: The efficacy of CD19 CAR-T cells in B-cell lymphoma patients is not as good as that in B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL) patients. This might be attributed to the intricate tumor microenvironment of B-cell lymphoma, which leads to CAR-T cell exhaustion, inability to sustain function, and difficulty infiltrating into the tumor interior.

pmc-12585606.title: Harnessing Total Scattering Techniques to Examine Local and Average Structure in Li/Mn Rich Cathodes
pmc-12585606.creator: Megan Murphy, Jue Liu, Boyu Shi, Gihan Kwon, Subhadip Mallick, Eungje Lee, Jason Croy, Michael Thackeray, Mahalingam Balasubramanian
pmc-12585606.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). A deep understanding of the structure of battery materials is crucial for achieving desired performance characteristics. Here, we outline the use of total scattering techniques as a powerful tool to investigate Earth-abundant cathode active materials (EaCAM). Just as X-rays and neutrons provide complementary insight, by examining both the local and average structure, total scattering gives rise to a comprehensive view of a material's atomic arrangement.

pmc-12729800.title: Seasonal Variation in the Diet Composition of Wild Boars (Sus scrofa) Based on Fecal DNA Metabarcoding in Bukhansan National Park, Republic of Korea
pmc-12729800.creator: Sanggon Lee, Manh Ha Nguyen, Wonjong Han, Misong Kim, Jiyoung Kim, Euikyeong Kim, Keumchul Shin
pmc-12729800.description: Simple SummaryWild boars are omnivorous animals, and their primary food sources vary based on their habitat. They mainly consume plants, but their diet also includes some animals and macrofungi. This study analyzed the food composition of wild boars during different seasons using metagenomic analysis of fecal samples.

pmc-13238615.title: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance–Based Urinary Metabolic Profiling for Assessing Heat Stress–Related Incident Kidney Injury in Health‐Care Workers
pmc-13238615.creator: Cheng‐Yu Ting, Chi‐Tsung Chen, Tzu‐Hsin Yen, Jason Kai Wei Lee, Sheng‐Han Lee, Shang‐Jen Chang, Tzu‐Han Hung, Hao‐Jan Liang, Hsiao‐Yu Yang, Ching‐Yu Lin
pmc-13238615.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). During the COVID‐19 pandemic, heat stress (HS) was a serious occupational risk for health‐care workers (HCWs) wearing personal protective equipment, which limits heat dissipation and increases the risk of kidney injury. In this exploratory study, we assessed HS‐related changes in the urinary metabolites of 38 HCWs working at mobile COVID‐19 screening units in Taiwan and their possible role in incident kidney injury (IKI). Urine samples were collected before and after their shifts.

pmc-13675726.title: Symptom Profiles Compatible With Disorders of Gut‐Brain Interaction in Individuals With Coeliac Disease on a Long‐Term Gluten‐Free Diet
pmc-13675726.creator: Tom van Gils, Hans Törnblom, Floris van Overveld, Olafur S Palsson, Ami D Sperber, Shrikant I Bangdiwala, Inês A Trindade, Marc A Benninga, Gerd Bouma, Magnus Simrén
pmc-13675726.description: BackgroundPersistent gastrointestinal (GI) symptoms are frequently reported in patients with coeliac disease (CD). Knowledge about the role of disorders of gut‐brain interaction (DGBI) as the cause of these persistent symptoms remains limited.ObjectiveTo assess the prevalence and factors associated with DGBI‐compatible symptom profiles in individuals with CD on a long‐term gluten‐free diet (GFD).

uslaw-usc-t12-s5003.title: 12 U.S.C. § 5003 — General provisions governing substitute checks
uslaw-usc-t12-s5003.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t12-s5003.description: United States Code, Title 12 (Banks And Banking); Chapter 50 (Check Truncation). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) No agreement required A person may deposit, present, or send for collection or return a substitute check without an agreement with the recipient, so long as a bank has made the warranties in section 5004 of this title with respect to such substitute check.
